passage: Note from Rekha, playgroup, Friday. Harsha (13 months) watched me drop a cloth over his rattle. Two weeks ago he would lose interest at once. Today he pulled the cloth off and shook the rattle at me, grinning. When I hid it under a cushion instead, he lifted the cloth first, frowned, then checked the cushion. I'll keep playing this with two hiding places and tell his grandmother about the game. 🙂

qa.q: What did Rekha hide under the cloth?
qa.a: Harsha's rattle.

qa.q: What does Harsha's frown after lifting the empty cloth suggest?
qa.a: He expected the rattle to be there and was puzzled not to find it.

qa.q: Why is Rekha's plan of two hiding places a good next step?
qa.a: It lets Harsha practise searching further while keeping the game simple and fun.

qa.q: How might Harsha's grandmother use the note?
qa.a: She could play the same hiding game at home and enjoy seeing him search.

grounding: Shows a baby now searching for a toy hidden under a cloth instead of losing interest.

passage: Kashish is folding quilts in the back room of their house in the kasba when Chaitanya, her son, eighteen months, toddles in with his wooden cow. She tosses a quilt over it as a joke. He stares at the lump. Then he tugs the quilt corner, digging with both hands until the cow's head pops out. "Moo!" he shouts. She hides it again under a pillow; he goes straight to the pillow and lifts it.

qa.q: Which toy did Chaitanya bring in?
qa.a: His wooden cow.

qa.q: Why did Chaitanya dig at the quilt?
qa.a: He believed the cow was still under it and was eager to get it back, and his "Moo!" shows how delighted he was to find it.

qa.q: How could Kashish turn this into a regular game?
qa.a: She could hide the cow in easy places during chores and cheer when he finds it.

qa.q: What is it like for Kashish when Chaitanya finds the cow?
qa.a: Her joke turns into a small shared game, and she gets to watch him work it out.

grounding: Shows a toddler knowing a toy under a quilt is still there and searching for it.

passage: Rosa, one and a half, sits on her grandmother Ada's bed in Lisbon while Ada hunts for her glasses. Rosa has been jingling Ada's keys. Ada lays the blanket over them to keep them quiet. Rosa looks at the bump, then crawls over and flips the blanket back. The keys jingle again. She laughs, covers them herself, and uncovers them, over and over, watching Ada's face each time.

qa.q: What did Ada lay the blanket over?
qa.a: Her keys.

qa.q: What does Rosa covering and uncovering the keys herself suggest?
qa.a: She seems to enjoy knowing the keys are still there, and to be testing it again and again.

qa.q: What could Ada do to make the moment playful?
qa.a: She could ask, "Where are the keys?" and cheer when Rosa finds them, turning it into peekaboo.

qa.q: Why might Ada be less pleased than Rosa at first?
qa.a: She wanted the keys quiet while she looked for her glasses, so the jingling may feel noisy.

grounding: Shows a toddler understanding covered keys still exist and uncovering them.

passage: I'm Francis, Ishita's older brother. Today I played with Ishita, eleven months, in the living room. I hid her rattle under a blanket while she watched. She stared at the blanket, then reached out and pulled it off. There was the rattle! She shook it and laughed. I hid it again under a pillow. She crawled straight to the pillow and lifted it. She knows it's still there.

qa.q: Where did Francis hide the rattle the second time?
qa.a: He hid it under a pillow.

qa.q: What does Ishita's laughing after finding the rattle suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she was pleased and excited to find it where she expected.

qa.a: He could hide the rattle under one of two covers so she has to remember which one.

qa.q: How does Francis see Ishita's new skill?

grounding: Shows an observer noticing a baby understanding a hidden object still exists and searching for it.

passage:
Monday: Salma, nine months, watches her father Sumit cover her toy duck with a cloth. She looks away, as if it's gone.

qa.q: What does Salma's beaming suggest about how she feels on Sunday?

qa.q: What helped Salma learn that the duck still existed?

qa.a: He probably feels proud and happy, seeing her understanding grow.

passage: Bhavna's father Harsha was folding clothes on the bed in their Hyderabad flat when she crawled up with her rubber elephant. He dropped a towel over it. Bhavna, fourteen months, stared at the towel, then at him. She grabbed the corner, pulled, and found the elephant, squealing. He hid it again, this time under a pillow. She lifted the towel first, frowned, then lifted the pillow and grinned.

qa.q: Where did Harsha hide the elephant the second time?
qa.a: Under a pillow.

qa.q: What was Bhavna feeling when she found nothing under the towel?
qa.a: She seemed puzzled and a little frustrated, which shows she was sure the elephant was still somewhere.

qa.q: How could Harsha make this game a little harder next time?
qa.a: Hide the elephant under one of three cloths while she watches, so she has to follow where it went.

qa.q: What is it like for Harsha to play this game while folding?
qa.a: It turns a chore into a fun game, and he gets to watch her thinking at work.

grounding: Shows a toddler searching under a towel and then a pillow for a toy she knows is still there.

passage:
"Where's the ball, Ujjwal?" Jasleen asked, tucking it under the quilt.
Ujjwal looked at the lump. "Baw."
"Where did it go? Gone?"
He patted the quilt, found the lump, and pushed his hand underneath. "Baw!"
"You found it! Okay, now watch Didi." She slid it under the pillow instead.
He went straight back to the quilt, lifted it and frowned.
"Not there, is it?"
He stared at her hands, then at the pillow, and crawled towards it slowly.

qa.q: Where did Jasleen hide the ball first?
qa.a: Under the quilt.

qa.q: What does Ujjwal's frown at the empty quilt suggest?
qa.a: He was confused and a little disappointed, since he expected the ball where he found it last time.

qa.q: What could Jasleen do to help Ujjwal succeed at the harder hiding?
qa.a: Hide it more slowly while he watches, and say "under the pillow" as she does it.

qa.q: What would change if Jasleen had just handed Ujjwal the ball?
qa.a: He'd get the toy, but he wouldn't practise searching for something he can't see.

grounding: Shows a toddler searching for a ball hidden under a quilt and working out where it moved.

passage:
Day-care note, Sachin, Lohri week
Because of the cold, we played indoors under shawls all morning. I hid a rattle under the red shawl while Akash (22 months) watched. He pulled it off right away. When I moved it under the blue shawl, he checked the red one first, then the blue. Later, on his own, he hid the rattle under his jumper and asked "Where?" with a big grin. I told his mother at pick-up; she laughed and said he hides her keys too.

qa.q: What did Sachin hide under the red shawl?
qa.a: A rattle.

qa.q: What does Akash's big grin when he hid the rattle suggest?
qa.a: He was proud and amused, enjoying turning the game around on Sachin.

qa.q: How could Akash's mother use this new game at home?
qa.a: She could hide his toys under a cloth for him to find, so the game stays fun and her keys stay safe.

qa.q: How does Sachin see Akash checking the red shawl first?
qa.a: As a normal step: Akash knows the rattle still exists but still looks where it was last.

grounding: Shows a toddler finding a rattle hidden under shawls and then hiding it himself, noted by a carer in winter.

passage: On a foggy January morning in their village near Mathura, everyone stayed under the razai. Then he flung the quilt back with both hands, grabbed the rattle, and shook it triumphantly. Vandana hid it again, deeper. Jatin crawled after it, burrowing and giggling.

qa.q: Where did Vandana hide the rattle?
qa.a: Under the edge of the quilt.

qa.q: How did Jatin feel when he found the rattle?
qa.a: Jatin felt triumphant and delighted, shaking it proudly.

qa.q: How did Vandana make the game grow with Jatin?
qa.a: She hid the rattle deeper the second time, a slightly harder search.

qa.q: How might Vandana feel as Jatin burrows and giggles?
qa.a: Vandana probably enjoys it, happy and amused, seeing him understand that the rattle is still there.

grounding: On a foggy winter morning, a baby searches under a quilt for a hidden rattle.

passage: At Lunar New Year in Toronto, Bao hid a red envelope under a cushion while his son Kwame, thirteen months, watched from the rug. Kwame looked at the cushion, then at his father. Bao waited. Kwame crawled over, pushed the cushion with both hands, and grabbed the envelope. He waved it, crackling, and laughed. His grandmother clapped from the sofa. Then Kwame put the envelope back under the cushion himself and looked up: your turn.

qa.q: What did Bao hide under the cushion?
qa.a: A red envelope.

qa.q: What did Kwame's look up after hiding the envelope suggest?
qa.a: Kwame was excited and wanted to keep playing, inviting his father to take a turn.

qa.q: How can Bao build on this game?
qa.a: Hide the envelope under two cushions or a blanket, and let Kwame hide things for him to find too.

qa.q: How might Kwame's grandmother feel clapping from the sofa?
qa.a: She probably feels delighted and proud, enjoying the family game during the festival.

grounding: At Lunar New Year in Canada, a toddler finds an envelope hidden under a cushion and turns it into a game.

passage: I'm Gurleen. In the summer holidays I help the aunty next door with her daughter Uma after lunch. Uma is fourteen months. Yesterday I hid her squeaky duck under my dupatta while she watched. She stared at the dupatta, then pulled it off my lap and squeaked the duck at me. So I hid it behind my back. She crawled round me until she found it. I think she knows now that things don't just vanish.

qa.q: What toy did Gurleen hide?
qa.a: Uma's squeaky duck.

qa.q: What might Uma have felt when she squeaked the duck at Gurleen?
qa.a: Uma seemed pleased and proud of finding it, perhaps even teasing Gurleen with it.

qa.a: Gurleen hid the duck out of sight instead of under the dupatta, which made Uma search around and stretched her understanding.

qa.q: How might Uma's mother feel about Gurleen's help?
qa.a: Uma's mother would likely feel grateful and relieved to have Gurleen playing with Uma on hot afternoons.

grounding: A young neighbour describes a toddler searching for a hidden toy on hot summer afternoons.

Then his cousin Sonali hid it under a cushion instead. Thomas lifted the blanket first, frowned, and started patting the other cushions until he found it. Sonali clapped and hid it again.
